independent_acceptance.conclusion: All three reported local defects remain Minor after independent checks of admissibility and repair. The fixed-period rank and complete ambient-isometry exclusion remain Needs Evidence; neither is promoted to a false main existence theorem.

problem_checks.source: PDF pp17?20 Definition1, signed-root convention, Definition2 and Lemma1
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: For g=(4cos x+cos2x)/5 and G=(4/5)sin x+(1/10)sin2x, the analytic A=(2sqrt2/5)sin(x/2)sqrt((cos x+3)((cos x+1)^2+1)) has A^2=1-g^2 and is antiperiodic under 2pi. Hence w=w0+lambda G(v/lambda) has period V=2pi lambda while its admissible signed root a=A(v/lambda) does not. For small lambda the image remains strictly in the allowed strip. The verified determinant 4a^2 w' det(i,F,F_w) gives generic planes on a suitable open interval. The frame has Phi(V)=1+lambda C+O(lambda^2), C!=0, and Phi(2V)=1+O(lambda^2). A noncollinear profile point does not commute with C, so the piece is not already closed and the asserted k=2 monodromy differs at first order.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: The source expressly permits sign-changing analytic roots; this is not a principal-root convention error. Requiring a common period of w and a restores ODE monodromy; twice a period suffices, with any already-closed/zero-angle endpoint handled separately. The actual spherical branch and angle perturbation have that stronger common-period property, so this example does not defeat them.

problem_checks.source: PDF p21 Theorem5; p47 Theorem10 and pp17?19 admissibility
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: The positive analytic E(w)=e^h(omega,w) is nonconstant, as its meromorphic theta expression has a noncancelled pole at w=2i omega. Choose admissible generic r<t with E(r)!=E(t), and w(v)=(r+t)/2+(t-r)tanh(v/L)/2, L>(t-r)/2. It is real analytic, has |w'|<1 and a positive analytic root, and its global frame exists on a compact parameter interval. The transformed u-metric coefficient H(v)=(1+R(omega)^2)^2/E(w(v))^2 has distinct limits at plus and minus infinity. A v-translation period would make H periodic; a continuous periodic function with a limit is constant. Thus the claimed translation period fails for allowed cylinders.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: The u-period and immersion formulas survive. The actual later torus-generator assumption supplies closed differential data and opposite remaining periods. Periodicity of w alone would not suffice. The torus-specific existence argument is not refuted.

problem_checks.source: PDF p44 nonzero-edge definition; p46 Proposition7
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: The global square net f(n,m)=(2n-1)i+2mj with f*=ni/2-mj/2 has nonzero edges and cross-ratio -1 on every quad. At epsilon=1 the edge -i to i has dual increment i/2; (1+i)(i/2)(1+i)=-1 and (-1+i)(i/2)(-1+i)=1, so both transformed imaginary parts vanish. The general squared output length is ((epsilon^2+a dot b)^2+|a cross b|^2)/|b-a|^2, giving the exact additional noncollapse condition.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: Quad closure is still correct and the formulas integrate to vertex maps. The defect concerns the stated nonzero-edge net conclusion; excluding a cross b=0 and a dot b=-epsilon^2 restores that conclusion. No collapse in the shown compact examples or failure of smooth immersion is inferred.

independent_acceptance.retained_scope: The actual fixed-period endpoint-map linearization supplies densities, but their independence has neither been proved nor refuted. The varying-period spherical rank is not automatically the required fixed-period rank. Breaking the displayed reflection does not alone exclude every ambient congruence with domain reparametrization, but no actual congruence counterexample was found. Both remain Needs Evidence. Analytic and finite diagnostics are distinguished, external classification/converse foundations are not fully reproved, and missing original code is not treated as a defect.
